activity.role: 11th head of Hongan-ji and Ikkō-ikki resistance leader
activity.notes: Kennyo succeeded as the eleventh head of Hongan-ji in 1554. Hongan-ji at Ishiyama was the principal fortified institutional center of the wider Ikkō-ikki/Hongan-ji network, which was not a single centralized state. The Activity closes in 1580 when Kennyo accepted the imperial-mediated peace with Oda Nobunaga and withdrew from Ishiyama; his later continuation as Hongan-ji religious head is not represented as continuing rule over an 'Ikkō-ikki state'.

sources.title: 戦国期本願寺教団の構造 — NDL Search / Shigaku
sources.citation_text: The academic study analyzes the Sengoku Hongan-ji organization and emphasizes the negotiated structure between the Hongan-ji head and the monto, supporting treatment of the Ikkō-ikki network as a religious-political organization rather than a unitary clan state.

sources.title: Hongan-ji Kennyo — Samurai Archive
sources.citation_text: The biography records Kennyo as the eleventh head of Hongan-ji from 1554 and his ten-year Ishiyama conflict with Nobunaga ending with withdrawal in 1580.
